question: A city puts speed cameras at its worst accident blackspots. Accidents there fall the following year. What is the safest reading?
options: Some of the fall would have happened anyway
The cameras made drivers worse elsewhere
answer: Blackspots are picked in their worst year, and an unusually bad year is usually followed by a less bad one whatever you do. Some of the improvement is real and some is the site returning to its normal rate — separating them needs comparison sites, not before-and-after.
move: A blackspot picked in its worst year would have eased on its own.
trap: A site is chosen because it had an unusually bad year.
source: Regression to the mean in road safety
reference: Hauer, Observational Before-After Studies in Road Safety, Pergamon, 1997
